body:
## What & why

A `/solve` launched by the Telegram bot in a detached `screen` session was
**OOM-killed (exit `137`)**, but the bot stayed alive and **never reported the
failure** — the job silently hung and the user was left waiting forever. The
captured log footer was unambiguous about the kill:

```text
Killed

==================================================
Finished: 2026-06-14 19:10:49.822
Exit Code: 137
```

…yet the bot kept treating the session as still running. The issue links **four**
concurrent `opus` sessions (at least one streaming large base64 PNGs under
`--attach-logs`), all reaped by the host OOM killer inside a single **40 ms**
window (`19:10:49.782` → `.822`) — the fingerprint of one host-level OOM cascade.
Every one of the four left an authoritative `Exit Code: 137` footer, and none was
reported.

## Root causes

- **RC-1 — liveness trusted over the recorded exit code (the upstream bug).** The
  external `start-command` CLI's `enrichDetachedStatus` re-derives a detached
  session's status from backend liveness (`screen -ls`). When a shell lingers
  after the wrapped command is already dead, `$ <id> --status` flips an
  already-completed record (`status: executed`, `exitCode: 137`) **back to
  `executing` and nulls the exit code** — never consulting the authoritative
  footer that `start` itself wrote. The bot's monitor only reacts to a _terminal_
  status, so the kill was never surfaced. Confirmed against upstream source and
  filed with a runnable repro as
  [link-foundation/start#134](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/134)
  (a regression of the fix for upstream #60/#101).
- **RC-2 — no durable registry.** The monitor's session registry was in-memory
  only; a bot restart orphaned every detached `/solve`.
- **RC-3 — no "last alive" marker.** No periodic heartbeat, so there was no way to
  bound which sessions were running when the bot was last alive, nor to pinpoint
  the exact moment of a total failure.
- **RC-4 — logs overwritten on restart.** The bot log could clobber the previous
  run, destroying the evidence needed to reconstruct the failure.
- **RC-5 — no "killed" vocabulary.** Completion messages classified outcomes as
  only success/failure, so a signal kill (137/143/139) looked like an ordinary
  non-zero failure (or nothing at all).

## Fix (defensive, consumer side — correct regardless of when upstream lands)

- **`src/session-status.lib.mjs`** *(new)* — shared, dependency-free status
  vocabulary: `normalizeExitCode`, `RUNNING`/`KILLED`/`FAILURE`, signal
  classification for 137/143/139/130, and predicates, so every call site agrees on
  what an exit code means.
- **`src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs`** — `parseSessionExitFooter` /
  `readSessionExitFromLog` read the **authoritative log footer**;
  `checkBackendSessionAlive` / `isSessionRunning` probe the real screen/tmux/docker
  backend. All verbose-traced.
- **`src/session-monitor.lib.mjs`** — when `--status` reports `executing`, it now
  cross-checks (a) the log footer [authoritative] and (b) a backend-liveness probe
  **gated by a 90 s minimum session age**, so a SIGKILL is reported instead of
  hanging while a just-started session is never misread. All three reconciliation
  branches are verbose-traced.
- **`src/session-store.lib.mjs`** *(new)* — durable registry: an atomic
  `sessions.json` snapshot plus an append-only, never-truncated
  `sessions-events.jsonl` audit log. Enables **resume** after a restart, reporting
  sessions killed while the bot was down — and only resuming sessions started
  **before** the bot's start time.
- **`src/bot-logger.lib.mjs`** *(new)* — every line is prefixed with an ISO-8601
  millisecond timestamp; structured `event()`/`heartbeat()` markers record "last
  alive"; logs **rotate, never overwrite** (the prior log is preserved as a
  timestamped backup; backups are pruned by policy). No data is destroyed.
- **`src/bot-lifecycle.lib.mjs`** *(new)* — heartbeat, resume-on-launch, and an
  orderly shutdown (which records a timestamped `bot_shutdown` marker so a clean
  stop is distinguishable from a hard kill) extracted from `telegram-bot.mjs` as
  pure, injectable factories.
- **`src/work-session-formatting.lib.mjs`** *(new)* + **`src/telegram-bot.mjs`** —
  completion messages now call out a **killed** outcome (❌ killed / signal)
  distinctly from an ordinary failure, and the bot wires the logger + store +
  heartbeat + resume + shutdown at startup.
- **`src/telegram-terminal-watch-command.lib.mjs`** — the **second location** of the
  same bug (found by the req #8 "fix in all places" audit). The live
  `/terminal_watch` loop decided "completed" purely from `--status`, so a session
  killed while `--status` still read `executing` would be **polled forever** with a
  misleading "running" snapshot — the #1927 silent-hang in the watch path. New
  `reconcileWatchCompletion` cross-checks the authoritative footer: once an
  `Exit Code:` is recorded it stops, corrects the displayed status to the real
  terminal one (e.g. `killed`), and a completed-but-failed session renders a ❌
  failure title instead of a ✅.

A `verbose` flag is threaded through every new status/footer/liveness/resume path
with explicit `[VERBOSE]` tracing (req #6), so the next failure leaves a trail.

## Requirements coverage (issue #1927)

| # | Requirement | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Detect a killed process via status instead of assuming success | footer-authoritative + liveness cross-check in `session-monitor` / `isolation-runner` |
| 2 | Detect a bot restart and resume sessions started before bot start | `session-store` + `resumeTrackedSessions` + `bot-lifecycle` |
| 3 | Start/end (or start-without-end) times everywhere; every log timestamped | `bot-logger` ISO-ms lines + `bot_shutdown`/`heartbeat` markers |
| 4 | Never destroy previous logs; bound resume to "last alive" | rotate-don't-overwrite + append-only events log + heartbeat |
| 5 | Compile data + deep case study | `docs/case-studies/issue-1927/` |
| 6 | Add debug/verbose output where data was insufficient | `[VERBOSE]` tracing across the new paths |
| 7 | Report the bug to the affected upstream repo | [link-foundation/start#134](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/134) + runnable repro |
| 8 | Apply the fix in all affected places | centralized in shared libs; every completion/monitor path routed through them. Full call-site audit in the case study — also fixed the `/terminal_watch` loop; cleanup/`/log` deliberately left as-is (their non-terminal default is the safe behavior, documented). |

## Reproduction

The upstream flip is reproduced by
`experiments/upstream-start-enrichDetachedStatus-flip.mjs`, which copies the three
relevant functions **verbatim** from `start`'s `status-formatter.js` and runs them
against a real lingering `screen` session:

```text
$ node experiments/upstream-start-enrichDetachedStatus-flip.mjs
log footer exit code              : 137
BEFORE enrichDetachedStatus       : status=executed exitCode=137
AFTER  enrichDetachedStatus       : status=executing exitCode=null
❌ BUG REPRODUCED: a completed exit-137 record was flipped back to "executing" and its exit code erased.
```

The consumer-side detection is covered by `tests/test-issue-1927-killed-detection.mjs`
(the `executing` status is reconciled to `killed` via the footer).

## Tests

- `npm test` — all **263** new assertions pass across 9 suites:
  - `tests/test-issue-1927-session-status.mjs` (51)
  - `tests/test-issue-1927-log-footer.mjs` (18)
  - `tests/test-issue-1927-completion-labeling.mjs` (30)
  - `tests/test-issue-1927-killed-detection.mjs` (25)
  - `tests/test-issue-1927-session-store.mjs` (29)
  - `tests/test-issue-1927-resume.mjs` (21)
  - `tests/test-issue-1927-bot-logger.mjs` (43)
  - `tests/test-issue-1927-bot-lifecycle.mjs` (29)
  - `tests/test-issue-1927-terminal-watch-kill.mjs` (17)

> Note: `tests/test-fable-5-model-support.mjs` reports 5 failures **locally on Node
> 20**, but it is **pre-existing and unrelated** to this PR — the three source files
> it loads (`src/models/index.mjs`, `src/claude.lib.mjs`, `src/config.lib.mjs`) and
> the test itself are **byte-identical to `main`** on this branch, and it passes on
> CI's Node 24. (Fable/Mythos model area, separate from #1927.)

## External update

- Filed [link-foundation/start#134](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/134)
  with a reproducible example, a consumer workaround (read the log footer directly),
  and a suggested fix (consult the footer before flipping `executed` → `executing`).

## Case study

`docs/case-studies/issue-1927/` contains the full analysis: a one-line summary,
preserved `source/` artifacts (issue JSON + **all four** killed-session logs the
issue links — gz + quick-read excerpts, one `temp_clone_token` redacted),
external research, the reconstructed timeline (all four sessions OOM-killed inside
a 40 ms window), all 8 requirements, the 5 root causes, per-requirement proposed
solutions, the implemented solution, and residual notes.

Closes #1927.

… (#1927)

Add a dependency-free session-status vocabulary (src/session-status.lib.mjs)
that maps a raw process exit code to a signal/kill label and classifies status
strings as running / terminal / failure / kill. 137 (128+SIGKILL) and 139
(SIGSEGV) read as kills; 143 (SIGTERM) and 130 (SIGINT) read as orderly
terminations.

reader (parseSessionExitFooter / readSessionExitFromLog) and backend-liveness
probes (checkBackendSessionAlive). start-command writes 'Exit Code: N' to the
log from the command's own close handler, so the footer proves termination even
when '$ --status' is stuck on 'executing' (the lingering-shell flip behind the
unreported OOM kill in #1927).

commits.messageBody:
… (#1927)

Fixes the core bug: a detached /solve was OOM-killed (exit 137) but `$ --status`
kept reporting `executing` — a lingering shell held the screen session alive, so
start-command's enrichDetachedStatus flipped the completed executed/137 record
back to executing (nulling the exit code). The bot stayed alive and NEVER reported
the failure; the session silently vanished.

session-monitor now cross-checks a stuck `executing` status two ways before
trusting it (req #1):
  1. read the authoritative exit footer the command itself wrote to its log
     ("Finished: ... / Exit Code: N") — wins outright when present; and
  2. probe real backend liveness (screen/tmux/docker), gated behind a 90s minimum
     session age so a just-launched session whose backend has not registered yet
     is never falsely declared dead.
When the `$ --status` record has been garbage-collected (exists:false) the monitor
falls back to the same liveness probe + persisted-log footer, so a session killed
while the bot itself was down is finally reported on resume rather than vanishing.

work-session-formatting labels the outcome three ways — killed (signal) vs failed
(non-zero) vs success — and recovers the true 137 from the footer when the status
record nulled it, instead of emitting a misleading generic "(exit code: 1)".

telegram-bot wires the durable store + timestamped logger, stamps BOT_START_TIME,
emits a periodic heartbeat, resumes tracked sessions on launch (only those started
before bot start, req #2), and flushes a final marker on shutdown signals (req #3).

Tests: 25 (killed-detection, the regression) + 30 (completion labeling) + 21 (resume).

commits.messageBody:
When a detached /solve is OOM/SIGKILL-ed, the surviving parent (the
Telegram bot, or /hive) now reports a ready-to-run
`solve <url> ... --resume <lastSessionId>` command in the killed-session
notification so the work can be picked back up. Addresses the PR #1928
review:

- "use the LAST of multiple sessions": a single /solve run prints many
  `Session ID:` markers (auto-continue, watch restarts, manual resume);
  the new session-resume.lib.mjs reads the LAST marker from the captured
  log tail (selectLastSessionId / readLastSessionIdFromLog), with a
  filesystem fallback (findLatestSessionLogId).
- which level resumes: the tool and /solve levels already resume via
  --resume on the child; the new behavior fills the top-level gap where
  the whole /solve job dies and the parent had no handle to resume.
- never storm / backward compatible: the bot SURFACES the command rather
  than auto-relaunching; planKilledSessionResume() bounds automatic
  resumes (default maxAttempts=1) for any caller that wants them. The
  resume section is additive via extraSections, only for killed /solve
  sessions, and wrapped so a planning error can never break the
  completion notification. `args` is now persisted so the resume command
  reproduces the original invocation; pre-existing sessions fall back to
  a reconstructed `<url> [--tool]` command.

Tests: test-issue-1927-session-resume.mjs (31 unit assertions) and
test-issue-1927-resume-notification.mjs (10 end-to-end assertions
driving the real monitorSessions).

… resume (#1927)

The killed-session resume block previously fell back to sessionInfo.sessionId
when the log had no 'Session ID:' marker. That id is the ISOLATION session id
(from generateSessionId()), a different namespace from the AI tool's --resume
id, so it would have produced a bogus 'solve --resume <isolation-id>' command.

Replace that fallback with findLatestSessionLogId() over the log directory's
<sessionId>.log files (those ARE tool session ids); offer no command when none
is found. Add an integration case asserting the isolation id never appears as a
--resume argument.

title: fix(telegram): detect OOM/SIGKILL-ed detached sessions + resume tracking after a bot restart (#1927)
